questions.question: Three agents each believe the next one owns a task, so they keep passing it on. Why won't a prompt like 'don't delegate in circles' fix it?
options: Each agent is acting reasonably; the failure is in the system, so it needs a runtime rule like a hop limit

questions.question: Two workers both start at the top of the same subtask list. What guard prevents the duplicate work?
options: Claiming (locking or leasing) a subtask before starting it
questions.explanation: One owner per subtask; a lease releases claims of crashed workers.

questions.question: Each agent splits its task between two helpers, five levels deep. How many calls did one request cost?
Why is an invented fact worse in a pipeline than in a single agent?
options: Later agents build on it, so it ends up looking well-supported in the final report
questions.explanation: Requiring sources at handoffs stops it at the first boundary.

questions.question: An agent reports 'All done!' and the run ends; the tests never ran. Which guard was missing?
options: Verifying completion against acceptance criteria before ending
questions.explanation: 'Done' is a claim to check, not a fact.

questions.question: The writer waits for review notes; the reviewer waits for a draft. What's the runtime fix, and the design-time fix?
options: A wait timeout with a fallback; and lint roles for mutual dependencies before running
questions.explanation: Timeouts break deadlocks; design reviews prevent them.
